2/22/2026 Previous Level: STAFF ONLYCurrent Level: STAFF ONLY / BITE QUARANTINEWhy did this level change?Cindy was routinely taking dogs out to the yard in 200, for out side time, When taking Ghost brown out he was already leash biting badly. She asked me to go with her to the courtyard to get him back inside. She gave him a toy and he took it, he played with it for a minute in the yard, and when she tried to get the leash around him he immediately released the toy and bit onto her glove. She had on bite gloves and bite sleeves. He would bite on to her glove and afer a min release, she tried to slide the leash over him but could not get it around his head, because he would not release his grip from her glove. I grabbed a catch pole sitting in the door way of 200, and tried to get it around him, that catch pole was broken. he immediately fixated on the bar of the catch pole. He would lunge and grab onto the catch pole , I was using the catch pole to block him from biting onto me, he was hyper fixating on everything and biting and not releasing. I blocked him from multiple different lunges, and cindy tried to slide another leash around his neck, that leash got caught halfway on his head, and he redirected and turned on her again. When he redirected I was able to grab another catchpole, and get it on him, while he was biting her. As soon as i secured the catch pole around his neck, he immediately released and walked back to his kennel. I held him in the corner while Cindy removed the leash and broken catch pole he had latched onto in the yard. He bit through her gloves and sleeves, multiple times.Behavior is declining. After the fact, I examined the first catch pole i tried to use, Thinking from the wrapping and padding around the pole, that it may be used as a bite stick, to prevent animal to human bites, when working with aggressive dogs. There was a working catchpole, in the outside door space right beside it.Bite Report and Quaratine started.

4/4/2024 Spanky Training/Handling Tips:? Drop off enrichment to help him expend some mental energy if possible before taking him out. (Frozen enrichment can be found in the white freezer located in the back sally port)? Before opening the kennel, show him your treats and ask him to “sit” and then give him a treat when he sits. If he’s excited, it  may take a few asks before he responds. Then use the treat on the other side of the loop trick to get the leash on him.? Keep treats visible as you walk and throw them on the ground for him to “find it” until you get outside or he shifts his attention to his surroundings ? If he bites at the leash, continue walking while ignoring the behavior. If you are in a contained area, intersperse dropping the leash in response to any increase in tugging. As soon as there is a slight pause or decrease in intensity, redirect him with “down” and/or “sit” and then give him a treat with verbal praise. Repeat as needed.? Start walking again, a treat + praise or throwing treat for him to "find it" every few steps ? If he starts to bite again, correct him by saying “eh” and then reset his behavior with “down” or “sit” followed by treat + praise. Then resume walking ? Once biting stops, keep him engaged and reinforce good walking with intermittent treats thrown for him to find? When un/re-leashing, first ask him to “sit” first and then give him a treat.  ** If you try to pull the leash away from him, he will tug back. If you ignore, drop the leash (he's not a runner), and redirect him with a command, then he will drop the leash to fetch the treat! ** Continue asking him to "find it" until he is leading the walk and no longer looking at you. At this point, he'll be easy on leash ** Any time you need to adjust/tighten/handle the leash, ask him to do something and reward him right as you do it (this results in him focusing on what you want him to do vs. the leash you're adjusting)

At one point when releashing him, he bit the leash but redirected immediately with “eh” + “sit” + treat and he didn’t bite it again. Walking on the trail, he was very easy on leash and enjoyed sniffing around.  I’ve detailed it in above notes but will list specific steps below and “pin” for easy reference. 4/4/2024 Spanky Training/Handling Tips:? Drop off enrichment to help him expend some mental energy if possible before taking him out. (Frozen enrichment can be found in the white freezer located in the back sally port)? Before opening the kennel, show him your treats and ask him to “sit” and then give him a treat when he sits. If he’s excited, it  may take a few asks before he responds. Then use the treat on the other side of the loop trick to get the leash on him.? Keep treats visible as you walk and throw them on the ground for him to “find it” until you get outside or he shifts his attention to his surroundings ? If he bites at the leash, continue walking while ignoring the behavior. If you are in a contained area, intersperse dropping the leash in response to any increase in tugging. As soon as there is a slight pause or decrease in intensity, redirect him with “down” and/or “sit” and then give him a treat with verbal praise. Repeat as needed.? Start walking again, a treat + praise or throwing treat for him to "find it" every few steps ? If he starts to bite again, correct him by saying “eh” and then reset his behavior with “down” or “sit” followed by treat + praise. Then resume walking ? Once biting stops, keep him engaged and reinforce good walking with intermittent treats thrown for him to find? When un/re-leashing, first ask him to “sit” first and then give him a treat.  ** If you try to pull the leash away from him, he will tug back. If you ignore, drop the leash (he's not a runner), and redirect him with a command, then he will drop the leash to fetch the treat! ** Continue asking him to "find it" until he is leading the walk and no longer looking at you. At this point, he'll be easy on leash ** Any time you need to adjust/tighten/handle the leash, ask him to do something and reward him right as you do it (this results in him focusing on what you want him to do vs. the leash you're adjusting)

3/14/2026  Behavioral information from Foster home.  Wanted to share my notes on Tucker as he goes into 2 full weeks in our home. Tucker is potty trained and crate trained. He initially whines or barks when you leave him in the crate but will settle within 30 minutes. His first 3 days he exhibited the same JM/LB behavior when he initially came out of the crate. He’s gotten a lot better and no longer shows extreme leash biting when he comes out of the crate.  He jumps on occasion but if you have your back towards him, he won’t jump and will sit to get your attention (and treats).  He is very treat motivated. We play fetch in the backyard to release some of his energy and get him some exercise. When he gets overstimulated (but not tired) he becomes very fixated on the ball and will jump and bite for the ball.  The nail trim has help avoid further scratches but when he is very stimulated he will put his mouth on your arms and pull.  I’ve started to use the squirt bottle to keep him from being jumpy bitey and I think he’s learning to control that. He has learned to play with plushy toys but prefers anything to chew on.  He doesn’t mind the muzzle, as much as any dog can tolerate it, but it’s easier to put it on. In general, I would not recommend him for a family with small kids due to his over excitedness and over stimulation.  He has not shown any negative reaction to our female dog - but she feels otherwise (particularly bc of the toys, she does not like to share). He can also be a little choppy when taking treats. He’s learning slowly how to take treats with a soft mouth, it’s even he gets overly excited the chomping can happen. We will try to walk him in our neighborhood to gauge his leash handling skills but I’m confident he’ll be fine.  He behaved very well on leash when I brought him to the shelter for his neuter surgery. I do want to see how over stimulated he can get when he plays fetch in the neighborhood dog park (no other dogs).   He is a good car rider, but we did clip him to the seat. He does need help getting into the car, still figuring out if the car is a safe place to be. He is smart and quickly knew which room was “his” and knows when to go into the crate. Let me know if you have any question or want specific videos to show his current behavior.

3/26/2026 "When Tucker gets overstimulated, he returns to his leash bitey and jumpy bitey behavior.  It is unfortunately a cause for concern for any potential adopter.  With regular exercise, it may curb the energy that gets stored up, but once he sees something he likes, he gets super fixated and will lock in and will want it.  This can be balls, plush toys, and leashes.  The fixation usually is triggered when he gets overstimulated.  Because he is smart, he remembers where I put things, like where I put the chuck it outside or where I place stuffies when I pick them up off the floor so he and Reese won’t taunt each other with it.  He will continually paw at the table storage where I keep the chuck-it balls.  He’s started to attempt to move the table storage to try to get to the chuck-it balls.  When he knows where I’ve placed the stuffies, he will attempt to reach for them.  He’s generally not destructive, but if there is an object that he wants, he will turn things over to look for it.We’ve started to walk in the neighborhood and he was generally doing okay, ignoring the leash and sniffing everywhere we go.  These past 2 walks he got excited by seeing other dogs, pulled strongly and when I pulled him back towards me he turned and went for the leash.  He only released when I did one squirt with the spray bottle.  On today’s walk, I did not have the spray bottle.  We met one of our young neighbors, middle school age, and though Tucker was friendly and accepted pets -
